frontier_question: Why did the United States move to force TikTok's sale or ban it between 2024 and 2025, and how was the dispute resolved?

chunks.content: The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act — signed by President Biden on 2024-04-24 — required ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90), or face a US ban. The Supreme Court upheld the law 9-0 (per curiam) on 2025-01-17, one day before the effective date of 2025-01-19. TikTok went dark in the US on 2025-01-18/19 (roughly 14 hours) and was restored 2025-01-19 after President Trump pledged to pause enforcement; his executive order of 2025-01-20 delayed enforcement for 75 days. The resolution was an Oracle-led deal (announced 2025-06-10 per Bloomberg) giving Oracle about a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations, with SoftBank and other investors participating; Vice President JD Vance led the White House negotiations, and ByteDance retained a majority interest. The national-security case rested on Chinese government access to US user data and the algorithm (CFIUS review, Project Texas hosting). The app stayed live, structured as a joint venture rather than an outright sale — "Project Texas": US user data in Oracle's cloud under US control — with the final ownership structure completed through 2025.

prior_gap_texts: The United States moved to force TikTok's sale or ban it primarily due to national security concerns, specifically the potential for Chinese government access to US user data and the platform’s algorithm [Source: ev-1].

Legally, President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on 2024-04-24, requiring ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90) or face a ban [Source: ev-1].
The Supreme Court upheld this law with a unanimous 9-0 decision on 2025-01-17 [Source: ev-1).
A subsequent executive order dated 2025-20 delayed enforcement further for 75 days [Source: ev-1].
The dispute was resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2025 June 10, which structured the outcome as a joint venture rather than an outright sale [Source: ev-1].
Under this agreement, Oracle received about a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations, with participation from SoftBank and other investors, while ByteDance retained a majority interest [Source: ev-1].
Vice President JD Vance led the White House negotiations that facilitated this resolution, ensuring the final ownership structure was completed through 2025 [Source: ev-1].
